EA TGQ.why: Electronic Arts' TGQ video codec, a real FFmpeg-supported format used in EA games; deep internals knowledge.

BFI.why: 'Brute Force & Ignorance' (BFI) video codec, a real named FFmpeg decoder; obscure, so Heisenbug fits.

AVUI.why: Avid's AVUI (Meridien-family) intermediate codec, a named FFmpeg decoder; specialist knowledge.

012v.why: Apple's uncompressed 4:2:2 10-bit codec, identified in FFmpeg and QuickTime docs by this FourCC; it's a named codec, though the name is a code, so this is a borderline keep.

Mimic.why: The Mimic video codec, a named FFmpeg decoder; deep-internals level.

Escape 124.why: The Escape 124 video codec, a named FFmpeg decoder used in Escape-engine titles; deep-internals level.

H.264.why: H.264/AVC, a standardized codec; nearly everyone knows it.

AVS3.why: Chinese AVS3 standard, a named codec in the AVS working group's specs and libuavs3d; specialists know it, so Race condition fits.

Interplay Video.why: Interplay's named video codec (FFmpeg interplayvideo decoder); deep-internals level.

EA MAD.why: EA's MAD video codec, a named FFmpeg decoder; deep-internals level.

DXV.why: Resolume's DXV codec, a named VJ/realtime codec in FFmpeg; specialist knowledge fits Race condition.

LEAD Video.why: LEAD Technologies made video codecs, but I can't confirm the exact name 'LEAD Video' as a codec kind from a source, so under the strict rule it's out.

Sorenson Video.why: Sorenson Video (SVQ1 / Sorenson Video 1 and 3), a named QuickTime codec; moderately known, so Null pointer exception fits.

DNxHD.why: Avid DNxHD, a named professional intermediate codec; domain-specialist knowledge fits Memory leak.

MagicYUV.why: MagicYUV, a named lossless codec used in FFmpeg and by its vendor; specialist knowledge fits Race condition.

BMV.why: Interplay's 'Discworld II BMV' video codec, a named FFmpeg decoder; deep-internals level.

CPiA.why: The CPiA (Vision) camera video codec, a named FFmpeg decoder; deep-internals level.

CYUV.why: Creative YUV (CYUV) codec, a named FFmpeg decoder; deep-internals level.

VVC.why: H.266/Versatile Video Coding is a real standardized codec, but it is much less known than HEVC or H.264, so Memory leak fits better than Null pointer exception.

HEVC.why: H.265/HEVC, a standardized codec that most video-literate people know.
